bib.title: Meta$^n$: Recursive Self-Improvement through Emergent Depth

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Meta^n: Recursive Self-Improvement through Emergent Depth", Zae Myung Kim, Young-Jun Lee, Seungyeon Jwa, Dongyeop Kang (Univ. Minnesota, SNU). Preprint, arXiv:2608.24735v1 [cs.AI], 25 Aug 2026 (first author Kim, Aug 2026). Code: github.com/minnesotanlp/meta-n.
COVERAGE: 22 PDF pages. Read the full extraction (main text, Appendices B-J) except the first part of Appendix B (comparison table; I read its prose) and the reference list, which I skimmed or skipped. No instructions found embedded. Figure image content not viewed, only captions and text.

FIT: Fits note 08 (self-improving loops, "updating the update method"). It names STOP, Godel Agent, DGM and HyperAgents, and it reframes "improve the improver" as "freeze the improver and grow its input". It also supports a verification note: the guard and rollback mechanisms. It is a preprint with a single group, a custom same-model setup, and an author-defined "meta-depth" metric, so label it as a claim of one paper.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Self-modifying agents all freeze a driver layer, which the authors say caps realized meta-depth at about 2.5. Meta^n keeps the operator Omega fixed and recurses on its input (traces of the stack below plus the code that produced them).
  number: ~2.5 (author-defined, half-credit scoring)
  setup: conceptual taxonomy (Sec 2.1, App B). Godel Agent's action API, DGM's archive maintenance and parent selection, and HyperAgents' outer evaluation loop are named as frozen.
  quote: "every system that does edit itself must hold some driver layer fixed for stability, capping realized meta-depth at ∼2.5"
  where: p2; Sec 2.1 p4; App B p15
- Removing recursion cuts archive-best validation score.
  number: 0.845 -> 0.714 (-0.131) Gemma CO-Bench; 0.886 -> 0.806 (-0.080) GPT-5.2 CO-Bench; 0.917 -> 0.759 (-0.158) GPT-5.2 AE Math
  setup: CO-Bench (36 NP-hard tasks), AlphaEvolve Math; depth-1 ablation (4 runs per seed, 3 seeds); scores are validation archive-best, no held-out pass.
  quote: "removing recursion from Metan drops CO-Bench archive-best validation from 0.845 to 0.714, a +0.131 gain from recursion alone"
  where: p3, Table 3 p12, App C p17
- Most of the recursion gain comes from the plain context string passed between layers, not from callable code.
  number: ~72% inter-layer context, ~15% code library, ~13% machinery (beam, retry, inspiration)
  setup: Gemma 4 31B-IT, CO-Bench, Table 3 (-0.094 for context, -0.020 for library)
  quote: "Removing the inter-layer context, a single string passed between layers, explains ∼72% of recursion's gain over a depth-1 baseline."
  where: p12
- Beats prior self-improving agents on all 8 benchmark families on at least one estimator.
  number: CO-Bench held-out Gemma 0.851 vs OpenEvolve 0.814 vs Godel Agent 0.451; GPT-5.2 0.870 vs 0.702 vs 0.527; LawBench 0.815 vs 0.745 vs 0.775
  setup: Gemma 4 31B-IT and GPT-5.2, mean over 3 seeds (42-44), archive-best estimator. On S2D the per-seed ranges overlap and the authors "do not claim significance". Godel Agent was run in a "corrected per-task" configuration.
  quote: "Meta n agentic leads every benchmark family in Tables 1 and 2 on at least one estimator, under both backbones"
  where: Tables 1-2 p7-8
- ARC-AGI-2 is the only benchmark where the baselines sit at the floor.
  number: 0.331±0.010 archive-best vs OpenEvolve 0.003 and Godel Agent 0.054 (dev score); best single chain 0.123, 1 seed
  setup: GPT-5.2 only, 120 tasks, pass@2, about $632 per Meta^n seed. The held-out text claims only Meta^n solves any task. I could not verify the held-out number, since it is in the text and not in a table.
  quote: "even Meta n's best single chain reaches only 0.123, but the full meta-level stack ... reaches 0.331"
  where: p8; App C p16
- Godel Agent does not catch up with more budget.
  number: 0.502 -> 0.615 (5x) -> 0.628 (10x) vs Meta^n 0.870 at 17M tokens
  setup: GPT-5.2, seed 42, CO-Bench held-out. The published GA interface scores about 0.000 because a single solver must cover all 36 tasks.
  quote: "raising GA's budget 5× and then 10× lifts held-out test only from that seed's default-budget 0.502 to 0.615 and 0.628"
  where: p10; App J p22
- Explanation for GA: with the driver fixed, the model must choose to modify itself and usually does not, while Omega always emits an injection.
  number: none (GA self-modification action invoked 4 times on S2D, 6 on LawBench, once on AE Math, once on CO-Bench, 0 on AlgoTune)
  setup: Gemma, published GA interface
  quote: "the model must choose to modify and usually does not, whereas Ω always emits an injection"
  where: p10; App J p22
- Deeper layers regress individual tasks, and the next Omega repairs them because it sees the code as well as the traces.
  number: d2->d3 mean lift -0.006; 41% of (chain, task) pairs strictly regress at depth 3; 18% drop below 0.8x of depth 2
  setup: code substrates; LawBench worked example 0.807 -> 0.773 -> 0.833
  quote: "41% of (chain, task) pairs strictly regressing at depth 3 and 18% dropping substantially (d3 <0.8· d2)"
  where: p11; Fig 3 p5
- Roles emerge with depth without prompting.
  number: rollback is 0% at depth 2 and 55% (code) / 33% (prompt) at depth 3; Cohen's kappa averages 0.59
  setup: 596 Omega emissions labelled by two LLM raters (GPT-5.2, Kimi-K2.6). Only agreed labels are counted, so the bars are lower bounds. Kappa is weakest on the abstract roles (0.30-0.37).
  quote: "Rollback is exactly zero at depth 2 in both substrates, under both raters, and appears at depth 3"
  where: p10, Fig 6, App E.3 p19-20
- Per-depth mean peaks at depth 3, but deep layers still win individual tasks.
  number: mean 0.726 at depth 3, 0.602 at depth 6; depth >=4 candidates win 31% of CO-Bench tasks
  setup: Gemma, code substrates
  quote: "Mean score per depth peaks at depth 3 ( 0.726) and falls to 0.602 by depth 6"
  where: p11
- Archive beats a single chain, and consolidation mode prevents regression.
  number: archive clears best chain by 0.06-0.07 on CO-Bench. Consolidation lifts per-task-best 0.502 -> 0.71±0.02 against a best-of-4 control at 0.61±0.03 (+0.10, 95% CI [+0.04,+0.16]), with zero regressions on 8 of 8 tasks.
  setup: 8-task CO-Bench band, 3 seeds, Gemma
  quote: "consolidation lifts per-task-best from 0.502 to 0.71±0.02 and beats a compute-matched best-of-4 control by +0.10"
  where: p11; App G p20
- Compute parity with OpenEvolve.
  number: S2D 0.732±0.023 vs 0.718±0.022; LawBench 0.784±0.013 vs 0.745±0.034; ~13x fewer candidate evaluations on CO-Bench (29 vs 378)
  setup: Meta^n token spend capped to OpenEvolve's budget, avg 485K tokens (Gemma). Full-budget Meta^n spends 10-20x more tokens than OE on the prompt benchmarks.
  quote: "Metan still leads at parity, S2D 0.732±0.023 vs. 0.718±0.022 and LawBench 0.784±0.013 vs. 0.745±0.034"
  where: p9
- Agentic mode costs 4-10x more tokens. Example: CO-Bench 5.3M single-shot vs 36.1M agentic.
  quote: "Token cost is roughly 4 to 10× higher in agentic mode (8 calls per task)"
  where: p9; Table 6 p17
- The gain depends on headroom and failure diversity. It is largest on CO-Bench (36 NP-hard shapes) and SR-matsci, small on S2D, and absent where the seed is strong: AlgoTune agentic ×15.10 vs single-shot ×18.47, and on SWE-Bench "Omega never activates".
  quote: "Ω's value therefore scales with both quantities, the headroom above the seed and the diversity of failure modes the archive can index."
  where: p12
- A single injected pre-process (no scipy) raised a pilot from 0.439 to 0.513.
  setup: 10-task pilot, CO-Bench
  quote: "improved mean score from 0.439 to 0.513 (+16.9% relative)"
  where: App F p20
- Stopping rule and design numbers: stop when Omega returns empty code, when P consecutive layers gain less than epsilon*R, or at max depth. epsilon=0.02, alpha=0.3, max depth 10 (TB2 4). Realized depths 3-6. Omega sees at most 20 traces at a 3:1 failure:success ratio. 65% of context goes to traces and 35% to the prior code stack. Generated code gets ast.parse checks, a dangerous-import check, a 10,000-char limit, and a smoke test before it is injected.
  quote: "Depth is therefore set by convergence rather than prescribed in advance; in practice no reported run reaches the cap."
  where: p6; App D p18; App E.2 p19

LIMITS (authors): same model at base and at every Omega, so a stronger improver over a weaker base is untested. They do not know whether the depth ceiling (3-6) comes from Omega's convergence or from reasoning capacity or context saturation, since both are "untested". The conditioning channel is a free-form string, and they suggest typing it. The Pi(k_d) vs Sum(k_d) coverage figure (27 vs 9) is an upper bound, "not a measured count". Compute is unequal on most benchmarks. TB2 has no baselines. The GPT-5.2 TB2 run is single-seed, and the Godel Agent baseline uses a self-corrected config. The AE Math pool size differs by system (10 to 16 problems). LawBench and AlgoTune were not run on GPT-5.2. Held-out S2D is 0.725 vs dev 0.887. The "meta-depth ~2.5" scale is the authors' own accounting. HyperAgents is classed from its own text ("cannot be altered", its Sec 7) and the paper does not test it. Consolidation is a small study.
BUILDS ON: Madaan 2023 (Self-Refine), Shinn 2023 (Reflexion); Schmidhuber 2003 (Godel Machine); Zelikman 2024 (STOP, "a single meta-step"); Yin 2024 (Godel Agent); Zhang 2025a (Darwin Godel Machine); Zhang 2026 (HyperAgents); Hu 2025 (ADAS); Zhang 2025b (AFlow); Romera-Paredes 2024 (FunSearch); Novikov 2025 (AlphaEvolve); Sharma 2025 (OpenEvolve); Fernando 2024 (PromptBreeder); Agrawal 2026 (GEPA); Lee 2026 (Meta-Harness); Liu 2026 (EvoX); Hofstadter 1979 (strange loops).
CODE: none worth keeping as code. Omega's signature, Eq 1 (p5): Omega: ({tau_i^(d-1)}, [C_2..C_{d-1}], T, d) -> C_d = (f_pre, L). Composition, Eq 2: S_d = M_d(C_d, S_{d-1}) = M_d ∘ ... ∘ M_2 ∘ S_1. Parent sampling weight: w(c) ∝ S̄(c) + α/(1+children(c)). Algorithm 1 is on p19.
FIGURES: Fig 2 p3 (three paradigms: hand-crafted, self-referential, recursive n-layer; the best single picture for note 08). Fig 3 p5 (build-step and run-step on the LawBench example, 0.767 -> 0.807 -> 0.773 -> 0.833; the regression and rollback cycle). Fig 4 p9 (seed vs linear-best vs archive-best, single-shot vs agentic). Fig 5 p9 (convergence vs OE and GA). Fig 6 p10 (role mix by depth). Fig 1 p2 (overview).
PROBLEMS: extraction was clean text, but tables are flattened (read Tables 1-2 against the quotes). A few superscripts are garbled (Metan = Meta^n). Fig 3's score values (0.767, 0.807, 0.773, 0.833) come from the figure text, and the 0.767 base score is not repeated in prose. The paper is dated Aug 2026, so cite it as a very recent preprint.
